item.title: commandline: Introducing Microsoft-Decision-1, our model for fast decision-making
item.description:
Microsoft introduced Microsoft-Decision-1, a decision-scoring model for structured decision tasks. It is described as optimized for low latency and high quality, and positioned as outperforming both LLMs and other decision models.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — October 5
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s weekly release note says this update improves cross-account and cross-environment use, while adding more control over agent access and work management. The excerpt also references GitHub Copilot Claude Haiku, but no further details are included.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: CodeQL 2.27.2 improves C++, Go, Rust, and JavaScript analysis
item.description:
CodeQL 2.27.2 is available with a new C++ regular-expression parser and analysis improvements for C++, Go, Rust, and JavaScript. The update applies to the static analysis engine used by GitHub code scanning.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: Retirement: Azure Key Vault Secrets Provider Extension for Azure Arc enabled Kubernetes clusters
item.description:
Azure Key Vault Secrets Provider Extension for Azure Arc-enabled Kubernetes will be retired on October 9, 2027. Users should migrate to the Azure Key Vault Secret Store Extension before that date.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Managed StandardV2 NAT Gateway for AKS
item.description:
AKS now provisions and manages a StandardV2 NAT Gateway for clusters using an AKS-managed virtual network. For new clusters in supported regions with managedNATGateway outbound type, StandardV2 is the default managed NAT Gateway SKU.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: Post-quantum authentication: Why organizations should start testing certificate ecosystems now
item.description:
Microsoft says organizations should begin testing certificate ecosystems now to prepare for post-quantum authentication. The post highlights Microsoft’s PQC TLS Pilot Program as a way to validate readiness for future post-quantum TLS deployments.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server in East US 3
item.description:
Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server is now generally available in the East US 3 Azure region. The update announces regional deployment availability.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Copilot code review: New organization billing options and controls
item.description:
GitHub added billing and license controls for Copilot code review at the organization level. Organization owners can now bill code review usage to the org for members with Copilot licenses and manage related controls.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Triage role users or higher can now archive pull requests
item.description:
GitHub now allows users with the triage role or higher to archive and unarchive pull requests. Before this change, only repository administrators could perform this action.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: Retirement: Microsoft Dev Box will be retired on September 18, 2028
item.description:
Microsoft Dev Box will be retired on September 18, 2028. The closing-down process begins on September 14, 2026, after which the service will eventually be unavailable.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: Azure Deployment Environments will be retired on February 22, 2027
item.description:
Azure Deployment Environments will retire on February 22, 2027. The closing-down process begins on September 14, 2026, after which the service will no longer be available.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Exceptions in WAF for Azure Application Gateway and Azure Front Door
item.description:
Azure Web Application Firewall exceptions are now generally available for Azure Application Gateway and Azure Front Door. The feature lets customers exclude specific parts of a request from WAF inspection to reduce false positives.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Microsoft Agent 365 integration with Azure API Management
item.description:
Microsoft Agent 365 integration with Azure API Management is now in public preview. The integration connects centralized governance with runtime enforcement for MCP servers and tools.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Screen readers can navigate timelines as lists
item.description:
GitHub issue and pull request timelines are now exposed to screen readers as lists. Assistive technology can announce the list structure, item count, and current position while users move through a timeline.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Draft pull requests count toward pull request limits
item.description:
GitHub now lets repository maintainers configure pull request limits so draft pull requests are counted too. Before this change, draft PRs were excluded from those limits.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: Announcing: Multiparty private offers in Microsoft Marketplace expands to Hong Kong
item.description:
Microsoft Marketplace multiparty private offers are now expanding to Hong Kong. This lets partners procure third-party cloud and AI solutions for customers in the Hong Kong market through Marketplace.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Claude Haiku 5.5 in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
Claude Haiku 5.5 is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. GitHub describes it as a lightweight model for fast, high-volume tasks such as subagents, quick edits, and terminal work.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: ai: Azure Document Intelligence and Azure Content Understanding: a practical guide
item.description:
The post compares Azure Document Intelligence and Azure Content Understanding, focusing on extraction architecture, workload fit, layout capabilities, deployment options, and how to evaluate which service to use. It is a practical guidance piece rather than a feature announcement.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: commandline: Bringing local models and sandboxed tools to Windows and GitHub Copilot
item.description:
GitHub Copilot is adding support for deciding when to use on-device models versus cloud models on Windows. The update also mentions sandboxed tools, but no further details are provided in the excerpt.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Anyscale on Azure
item.description:
Anyscale on Azure is now generally available. It is a managed platform for running distributed Python workloads on Ray, deployed directly on Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) and integrated with Azure services.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Enabling the Bulk admin role for SQL Server on Linux
item.description:
SQL Server on Linux now supports the bulkadmin fixed server role and the ADMINISTER BULK OPERATIONS permission starting with SQL Server 2025 CU9 and SQL Server 2022 CU27. This enables bulk data import operations without requiring users to be members of the sysadmin role.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Purpose-built model for leaked secret detection
item.description:
GitHub announced a new purpose-built, context-aware model for leaked secret detection as part of Secret Protection. It is intended to improve secret detection in code workflows, including those that involve AI agents.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: 3 lessons from frontier AI vulnerability research
item.description:
Microsoft Security says its FORGE Lab is applying frontier AI methods to scale vulnerability research beyond Windows, including work on the Linux kernel. The post highlights three takeaways from that research effort.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Local sandboxing for GitHub Copilot now generally available
item.description:
Local sandboxing for GitHub Copilot is now generally available. It is supported in GitHub Copilot CLI, the GitHub Copilot app, and VS Code sessions using Agent Host.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Discover local models in GitHub Copilot CLI
item.description:
GitHub Copilot CLI version 1.0.94-0 adds a /model command so you can discover supported local models from within the CLI instead of leaving your workflow.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: devops+ai: 🔥Using Whisper, FFMPEG, and yt-dlp to Analyze Sermons for Red Flags🔥
item.description:
The article describes a toolchain using Whisper, FFmpeg, and yt-dlp to download sermon audio/video, transcribe it, and analyze the text for potentially bigoted or otherwise problematic language. It frames the approach as using AI to review sermons for “red flags.”

  • Source: Let’s do DevOps

item.title: github: Update your IDE to restore agent activity in Copilot usage metrics
item.description:
GitHub says some Copilot usage metrics showed declining agent activity and agent lines of code even as overall usage increased because of an IDE-related issue. A fix is rolling out, and users should update their IDE to restore correct agent activity reporting.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: Retirement: Pod name dimension in AKS pod platform metrics
item.description:
Azure Monitor is retiring the pod name dimension for certain AKS pod platform metrics starting September 30, 2027. These metrics will move to aggregate pod counters instead.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Stacked pull requests generally available
item.description:
GitHub stacked pull requests are now generally available. The feature lets you split large changes into smaller, focused pull requests that can be reviewed independently and merged together.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: Retirement: Azure App Service on Azure Stack Hub
item.description:
Azure App Service on Azure Stack Hub will be retired on September 30, 2029. From September 30, 2026, new installations are no longer supported and the product will receive no new releases, features, or enhancements.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: Support for Java 8, 11 and 17 will end on September 1, 2027
item.description:
Azure App Service will end support for Java 8, 11, and 17 on September 1, 2027. Apps will keep running, but security updates and customer support for those Java versions will stop.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: k8s: The Shift to cgroup v2 in Kubernetes: What You Need to Know
item.description:
Kubernetes is deprecating cgroup v1 and is moving toward cgroup v2 as the default path: in v1.35, kubelet startup fails by default on cgroup v1 nodes, and kubeadm preflight checks now error on v1.35+ when v1 is detected. The post also summarizes cgroup v2-related behaviors and features in Kubernetes 1.36, including Memory QoS, container-scoped OOM handling, PSI metrics, and in-place pod-level resource updates.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: dotnet: A faster, lighter C# Dev Kit
item.description:
C# Dev Kit has been rebuilt to open solutions in about one second and use significantly less memory. The post says it explains the changes behind those improvements.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: azure: Retirement: Always Encrypted with Intel SGX Enclaves
item.description:
Always Encrypted with Intel SGX enclaves in Azure SQL Database will retire on October 31, 2027. The retirement is tied to the phase-out of SGX-enabled DC-series hardware, and customers are directed to move to VBS enclaves.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: CISO perspectives on managing vulnerability risks in the age of AI
item.description:
The post says CISOs should adapt vulnerability management practices for AI-driven environments to reduce cybersecurity risk and improve resilience. It frames the topic as managing vulnerabilities in the age of AI-powered tooling and threats.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: AKS on bare metal now on Ubuntu
item.description:
Azure has a public preview for running AKS on bare metal using Ubuntu, aimed at on-premises Kubernetes deployments without a virtualization layer. The update highlights support for local control of hardware and software, with a focus on AI workloads.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Code scanning AI Scan enablement status in security overview
item.description:
GitHub added AI Scan for pull requests enablement status to the security overview coverage view for organizations and enterprises. The code scanning summary now indicates which repositories have AI Scan enabled or not enabled.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Secret scanning adds detectors for Lovable, Supabase, and more
item.description:
GitHub Secret Scanning added new detectors for secrets from Lovable Labs, Pydantic Services Inc., and Supabase. A new provider also joined the secret scanning partnership program.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure HorizonDB expands to additional regions
item.description:
Azure HorizonDB is now available in additional Azure regions in public preview. The expansion gives users more deployment options for PostgreSQL workloads closer to applications and users.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines in Azure Bleu
item.description:
SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines is now generally available in Azure Bleu. This lets customers deploy and manage SQL Server workloads in France’s sovereign cloud while meeting data residency and sovereignty requirements.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: k8s: Scaling Kubernetes Workloads with Node Swap
item.description:
Kubernetes node swap is now GA in v1.34, and this post reports that using fast NVMe Local SSDs for swap can raise pod density for memory-heavy workloads with little latency impact when active working sets remain in RAM.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: azure: Announcing: Table discovery in OneLake Catalog search
item.description:
Starting October 15, 2026, Microsoft Fabric search will return tables from semantic models, lakehouses, and mirrored databases as separate results in OneLake Catalog search. Users will be able to find tables by name, description, or an exact column-name match.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure Backup for PostgreSQL flexible server and elastic cluster (v2)
item.description:
Azure Backup for PostgreSQL flexible server and elastic cluster (v2) is now in preview. It uses physical backups from managed disk snapshots and stores them in an Azure Backup vault for long-term retention.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: IPv6 Support for Application Gateway WAF
item.description:
Azure Application Gateway WAF now supports inspection and enforcement for IPv6 traffic in Public Preview. This adds IPv6 support to the web application firewall layer.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: dotnet: UWP and WinUI 3 apps: UI testing with MSTest
item.description:
Microsoft describes how to run UI tests for UWP and WinUI 3 apps using MSTest and Microsoft.Testing.Platform. It covers testing across packaged, unpackaged, and AppContainer hosts.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: commandline: Beyond violation rates: Are your AI evaluations measuring the right things?
item.description:
The article argues that structured evaluation design can make AI evaluations more comprehensive and easier to interpret. It emphasizes measuring a wider range of behaviors and producing failures that are traceable and actionable.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: commandline: Building an agentic system and a learning loop around customer IP
item.description:
Microsoft and Kantar built an agentic system around Kantar’s 30 years of ad metrics and frameworks to evaluate and help optimize advertisements. The system is described as part of a learning loop for customer IP.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: github: Stateless GitHub App installation tokens rolled out
item.description:
GitHub has completed the staged rollout of the stateless GitHub App installation token format. By default, newly minted installation tokens now use the new format.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot code review: API support and new default effort level
item.description:
GitHub Copilot code review can now be requested through both the REST and GraphQL APIs, and each request can specify an effort level. The default effort level has changed to Balanced.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Unvalidated npm trusted publishing configurations now expire
item.description:
Unvalidated npm trusted publishing configurations now expire 48 hours after creation and can no longer authorize publishing. This reduces the risk of a repository or project name changing after the configuration is created.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: npm staged publishing now supports creating new packages
item.description:
npm staged publishing now supports creating new packages. You can create a new package with npm stage publish using either a local session or a granular access token, including a stage-only token.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Selected models in GitHub Copilot deprecated
item.description:
GitHub deprecated several Copilot models across all Copilot experiences on October 2, 2026. The change applies to Copilot Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Major version upgrades (MVU) for Azure Database for PostgreSQL elastic clusters
item.description:
Azure Database for PostgreSQL elastic clusters now support major version upgrades in public preview. Existing clusters can be upgraded in place to a newer supported PostgreSQL version without creating a replacement cluster or migrating distributed data.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: commandline: Azure Content Understanding: Building on lessons from a decade of Document Intelligence
item.description:
Microsoft reflects on a decade of document understanding work and how those lessons inform Azure Content Understanding. The piece emphasizes limits of LLMs in document reading and the importance of handling edge cases with confidence, grounding, and reasoning.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: commandline: LLM-as-translator pattern: Adding natural language understanding to an existing system without rewriting it
item.description:
The article describes using an LLM as a translation layer to add natural-language understanding to an existing system without rewriting it. The approach modernizes legacy implementations by inserting an abstraction layer instead of replacing core logic.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: github: New fields for SecurityAdvisory GraphQL API
item.description:
GitHub added five new fields to the SecurityAdvisory GraphQL object, allowing more of the GitHub Advisory Database to be read directly through GraphQL instead of using the REST API. The changelog notes one of the new fields as cveId.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Confidential comments on repository security advisories
item.description:
GitHub now supports confidential comments on repository security advisories. These comments are visible only to users with write access to the repository, allowing private discussion of a report.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Repository security advisory comments API in public preview
item.description:
GitHub has added REST API support for reading, adding, and editing comments on repository security advisories. The API also works for advisories created from private vulnerability reports.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Rate limits for private vulnerability reports
item.description:
GitHub is adding rate limits for private vulnerability reports to reduce low-quality and automated submissions that can obscure important reports. The change caps how many new reports a single account can submit.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Structured forms for private vulnerability reports
item.description:
Private vulnerability reports now support structured forms to collect the details needed for triage, including a reproducible proof of concept. This replaces reliance on a single free-text field with a more guided intake flow.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot can now interact with desktop apps with computer use
item.description:
GitHub Copilot computer use is now in public preview in Copilot CLI and the Copilot app on macOS and Windows. It can interact with desktop applications on the user’s behalf.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Actions: macOS 14 runner image retirement
item.description:
GitHub Actions will retire the macOS 14 runner image on November 2, 2026. Before removal, jobs that use macOS 14 will temporarily fail during scheduled awareness periods.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot in VS Code, September 2026 releases
item.description:
September 2026 GitHub Copilot in VS Code releases cover VS Code v1.136 through v1.140 and focus on streamlining agent-driven development from implementation through pull request merge. The update adds automations for repeatable tasks and agent merge support.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Accessibility statements highlighted on repository overview
item.description:
GitHub now highlights an ACCESSIBILITY.md file on the repository overview when it is located in the repository root, .github/, or docs/. The changelog entry also notes support for adding or proposing an accessibility statement file.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Actions retention now covers checks, runs, and statuses
item.description:
GitHub Actions retention now applies to checks, workflow runs, and statuses, using the same retention setting that already controls artifacts and logs. This means those records are now kept or removed according to the repository or organization Actions retention policy.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: aks: Release Notes 2026-09-25
item.description:
AKS release v20260925 adds GA identity bindings, preview support for Ubuntu 26.04 and Windows Server 2022 to 2025 OS SKU migration, and includes multiple behavioral changes, bug fixes, and component updates across Kubernetes versions. It also announces upcoming VMAS cluster auto-migration to VM node pools starting 2026-09-30 and notes that Windows Server 2022 is unsupported on Kubernetes 1.37+.

  • Source: Release notes from AKS

item.title: azure: Retirement: DCsv3 and DCdsv3-series Azure Virtual Machines will be retired on October 31, 2029
item.description:
DCsv3 and DCdsv3-series Azure Linux, Windows, and Dedicated Host virtual machines will be retired on October 31, 2029. After that date, they will no longer be available for use or purchase, so workloads should be migrated before then.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Scheduled code scanning skips inactive repositories
item.description:
Weekly scheduled scans for code scanning default setup and GitHub Code Quality now run only after a repository has had an analysis triggered by a push or pull request. Repositories with no recent activity no longer count toward scheduled scanning.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Code coverage uploads no longer fail CI for new branches
item.description:
GitHub Code Quality’s upload-code-coverage action no longer causes CI failures when coverage is uploaded from a branch that does not yet have an open pull request. This changes behavior from the previous failure case for new branches.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Dynamic workflows in Copilot CLI and the Copilot app
item.description:
Dynamic workflows are now available in Copilot CLI, the GitHub Copilot app, and the GitHub Copilot SDK. They let you define an orchestration in code.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Insights from the 2026 Microsoft Digital Defense Report
item.description:
Microsoft published a brief post pointing readers to highlights from the 2026 Microsoft Digital Defense Report. The note says the security environment is becoming more interconnected, but provides no detailed findings in the excerpt.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Preparing governments for an era of interconnected cyber risk
item.description:
Microsoft says government agencies and services were the most impacted sector in 2026 cyber activity, accounting for 27% of observed activity versus 17% in 2025. The post ties this to Microsoft’s 2026 Digital Defense Report and frames it as interconnected cyber risk for governments.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: SQL performance monitoring for SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines
item.description:
Microsoft has released a public preview of Microsoft-managed performance monitoring for SQL Server on Azure Virtual Machines. It lets you monitor SQL Server on Azure VMs without creating custom collection scripts or manually correlating telemetry.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Opt-in dist-tag permissions for npm trusted publishing
item.description:
npm trusted publishing can now optionally get permission to manage dist-tags using short-lived OIDC credentials. This covers actions like moving tags such as latest, next, and beta without using long-lived credentials.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: ​​Secure what’s next: Your guide to Microsoft Security at Microsoft Ignite 2026
item.description:
Microsoft’s Ignite 2026 security post says the company will highlight an AI-first, end-to-end security platform. The platform is described as covering identities, devices, data, applications, clouds, infrastructure, and AI agents.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: Retirement: NVv3-series Azure Virtual Machines
item.description:
Microsoft Azure retired several NVv3-series virtual machine sizes on September 30, 2026. Any remaining NVv3-series VMs are also being retired.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: NVv4-series Azure Virtual Machines
item.description:
Azure retired the NVv4-series VM sizes listed in the update, effective September 30, 2026. The retirement includes Standard_NV4as_v4 through Standard_NV32ahs_v4 variants.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Ubuntu 26.04 support in AKS
item.description:
AKS now has public preview support for Ubuntu 26.04 node pools through a new Ubuntu2604 OS SKU based on Ubuntu Minimal. The update is intended to help teams move with Ubuntu LTS releases while addressing package footprint, security, and compatibility concerns.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Announcing: Azure canvases for GitHub Copilot
item.description:
Azure canvases for GitHub Copilot are interactive shared workspaces that surface Azure tools, dashboards, and guided workflows alongside Copilot conversations. The update highlights using them to explore Azure resources, analyze costs, and build hosted skills.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: Dv3, Dsv3, Ev3, and Esv3 Azure VMs
item.description:
Microsoft announced retirement of the Dv3, Dsv3, Ev3, and Esv3 Azure VM series in public cloud regions. These VM families will reach end-of-life on November 15, 2029.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: GitHub Advanced Security trials for GitHub Team
item.description:
GitHub Team customers can now start self-serve trials of GitHub Advanced Security from an organization’s Overview page and Billing settings. The trial lets teams evaluate GitHub Code Security and GitHub Secret Protection.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: HydraFusion in VS Code and the GitHub Copilot app
item.description:
HydraFusion research preview is now available in Visual Studio Code and the GitHub Copilot app, expanding access beyond Copilot CLI. It appears in the model picker in both products.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Unauthenticated command injection on internet-facing mail servers: tracking CVE-2026-73570
item.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence reports active exploitation of CVE-2026-73570 in Zimbra mail servers. The post covers observed attack paths, ways to detect the activity, and mitigation guidance.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: X25519-only TLS ends for GHE.com on October 7
item.description:
Starting October 7, 2026, GitHub Enterprise Cloud with data residency (GHE.com) will stop accepting TLS connections from clients that support only X25519 for key agreement. Most customers are not expected to be affected.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Phishing Abuses RMM Tools for Persistent Access
item.description:
Microsoft reported phishing campaigns that abused MSP360 RMM to deploy ScreenConnect and establish redundant remote-access channels for later malicious activity. The focus is on persistence and follow-on access rather than initial compromise alone.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: ai: Why content extraction still matters in the GenAI era
item.description:
The post argues that as AI models improve, reliable content extraction becomes more important for trustworthy downstream use. It also contrasts Azure Content Understanding and Azure Document Intelligence, and previews what is next.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: azure: Retirement: Azure Functions v1 hosting model on Azure Container Apps
item.description:
Azure Functions v1 hosting model on Azure Container Apps will be retired on September 29, 2027. After that date, existing v1 apps will stop running and will no longer handle requests or event-driven triggers.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Storage optimized Lasv5 and Laosv5 Azure VM series
item.description:
Azure has generally available Lasv5 and Laosv5 storage optimized VM series, based on 5th Gen AMD EPYC (Turin). The series offers 2–160 vCPUs, 8 GiB memory per vCPU, and 720 GB of local NVMe disk per vCPU.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Automatic Zone Placement for Virtual Machine Scale Sets
item.description:
Azure has introduced a public preview of Automatic Zone Placement for Virtual Machine Scale Sets. Azure will automatically choose suitable availability zones based on SKU availability, capacity, and placement requirements, reducing the need to manage zone lists manually.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Repository custom runner settings for Dependabot
item.description:
Repository administrators can now set the runner type, optional custom label, and optional runner group for Dependabot version and security updates. This extends existing runner configuration options for Dependabot.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Arc-enabled SQL Server in Germany West Central
item.description:
Azure Arc-enabled SQL Server is now generally available in Germany West Central. It lets you connect SQL Server instances to Azure Arc for inventory, governance, security, assessment, and license management.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Arc-enabled SQL Server Available in Italy North
item.description:
Azure Arc-enabled SQL Server is now generally available in the Italy North region. Customers can connect SQL Server instances to Azure Arc to use Azure-based inventory, governance, security, assessment, and license management features.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Bring business context with external custom properties
item.description:
GitHub now supports external custom properties so repository business context can be synced from a system of record such as a CMDB, internal developer portal, or other in-house system. This lets teams attach external metadata to repositories more seamlessly.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Ultra Disk
item.description:
Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server now supports Ultra Disk in public preview. It is intended for I/O-intensive, transaction-heavy workloads that need consistently low latency.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: SQL Performance Monitoring for Azure SQL Database
item.description:
Microsoft has opened public preview of managed SQL performance monitoring for Azure SQL Database. It provides built-in monitoring so you do not need custom data collection scripts or manual correlation across separate tools.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Performance monitoring for Azure Arc–enabled SQL Server
item.description:
The public preview for performance monitoring of Azure Arc–enabled SQL Server adds more flexible ways to explore and visualize performance data. Users can query Microsoft-managed monitoring data directly through a telemetry endpoint.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure SQL updates for late-September 2026
item.description:
Azure SQL added larger Hyperscale Premium compute options in Azure SQL Database, including 160-vCore and 192-vCore SKUs. Microsoft says these provide up to 50% more compute capacity than the previous top tier.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server supports cross-tenant customer-managed keys (CMK)
item.description:
Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server now supports cross-tenant customer-managed keys (CMK). Data can be encrypted with keys stored in an Azure Key Vault or Azure Managed HSM in a different Microsoft Entra tenant than the PostgreSQL server.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public preview: Script-based deployment for SQL Server on Linux Azure VM
item.description:
Public preview of a script-based deployment flow for SQL Server on Linux Azure VMs. It replaces legacy marketplace images with automated provisioning and adds more flexibility and customization.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: SQL Server on Azure Local Disconnected (ALDO)
item.description:
Azure Local Disconnected (ALDO) for SQL Server is now generally available. It extends SQL Server support to disconnected environments that cannot maintain continuous Azure connectivity, including regulated, secure, remote, and air-gapped deployments.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: SQL Server support on Azure Local connected mode
item.description:
SQL Server support on Azure Local is now generally available in connected mode. It lets you run SQL Server workloads on Azure Local infrastructure while using Azure services for centralized management, governance, monitoring, security, and licensing.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure SQL updates for late-September 2026
item.description:
Late-September 2026 Azure SQL preview updates include Database Hub in Microsoft Fabric. The hub provides a unified experience for discovering, managing, monitoring, and optimizing databases across SQL Server and Azure SQL.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Database DevOps in SSMS powered by SQL projects
item.description:
SSMS now supports generally available Database DevOps using Microsoft.Build.Sql projects. This gives users a local definition of database objects to help implement, manage, and collaborate on database changes.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure SQL Database Hyperscale Serverless auto-pause and auto-resume
item.description:
Azure SQL Database Hyperscale Serverless now supports auto-pause and auto-resume in public preview. Databases can pause during inactivity and resume automatically when activity returns.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: SQL Formatter
item.description:
SQL Formatter is now generally available for Visual Studio Code, allowing SQL scripts to be formatted directly in the editor. It includes customizable formatting options to match preferred code styles.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: SQL Migration Agent Skills for assessment, migration, and validation
item.description:
SQL Migration Agent Skills are now generally available to help automate SQL Server to Azure migrations. They provide reusable AI-powered skills for assessment, target selection, migration execution, and post-migration validation.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: Azure Arc enabled System Center Virtual Machine Manager will be retired September 30, 2029
item.description:
Microsoft will retire Azure Arc-enabled System Center Virtual Machine Manager (SCVMM) on September 30, 2029. Customers using it should plan to transition to an alternative solution before that date.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Migrate directly from Azure Arc to Azure SQL Database, including Hyperscale
item.description:
Azure Arc database migration now supports Azure SQL Database, including Hyperscale, as a direct migration target in public preview. The guided workflow also handles Azure Database Migration Service and Self-hosted Integration Runtime setup.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Microsoft SQL Agent Skills
item.description:
Microsoft SQL Agent Skills are in public preview. They provide product-specific guidance for AI agents used to build, operate, and migrate SQL workloads across Azure SQL Database, Azure SQL Database container, and SQL Server migration scenarios.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Long-term retention (LTR) v2 for Azure Database for PostgreSQL
item.description:
LTR v2 for Azure Database for PostgreSQL is in public preview. It replaces LTR v1’s logical pg_dump/pg_restore backups with physical snapshot-based backups integrated with Azure Backup Vaults.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: Microsoft HPC Pack
item.description:
Microsoft is retiring all versions of HPC Pack. It is entering a one-year retirement period with limited retirement-only support, and end of support is August 27, 2027.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: Azure IoT Central will be retired on September 20, 2029
item.description:
Azure IoT Central will be retired on September 20, 2029. Microsoft says you can keep using it until then, but recommends starting transition planning early as Azure IoT evolves.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Support for large volume breakthrough mode
item.description:
Azure NetApp Files large volume breakthrough mode is now generally available. It adds support for volumes up to 2 PiB and throughput up to 80 GiB/s, depending on workload characteristics.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Storage with cool access enhancement
item.description:
Azure NetApp Files now supports QoS updates with cool access enabled on Premium and Ultra service levels, improving how performance and cost are balanced for mixed hot and cool workloads. Throughput automatically adjusts as data moves to cool storage to maintain hot-tier performance behavior.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview : Microsoft entra kerberos authentication for Azure NetApp Files
item.description:
Azure NetApp Files now supports Microsoft Entra Kerberos authentication for SMB volumes in public preview. It allows hybrid and cloud-only users to authenticate via Microsoft Entra ID using cloud-issued Kerberos tickets.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: GPT-6.1 Sol in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
GPT-6.1 Sol is now generally available and rolling out in GitHub Copilot. GitHub says it can be used for agentic coding and terminal workflows with strong multistep performance.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: ​​Beyond source code: A path to the keys to the kingdom
item.description:
Microsoft describes how Storm-3068 used a compromised identity to expand access into cloud environments, moving beyond source code exposure to broader infrastructure compromise. The post focuses on defensive steps for protecting identities, CI/CD pipelines, and cloud infrastructure.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: Star Blizzard refines phishing and malware delivery with the RedFlick technique
item.description:
Microsoft says it has observed Russian state actor Star Blizzard since January 2026 using large-scale phishing, compromised website accounts, and a new malware delivery method it tracks as RedFlick. The update focuses on the actor’s improved detection evasion and delivery techniques.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Vector search and vector indexes in Azure SQL
item.description:
Vector search and vector indexes are now generally available in Azure SQL Database. The update adds CREATE VECTOR INDEX and VECTOR_SEARCH T-SQL support for efficient approximate nearest neighbor searches in AI scenarios.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure SQL Dev Hub
item.description:
Azure SQL Dev Hub is in public preview as a central starting point for building applications with Azure SQL. It provides guidance for connecting from .NET, Python, Node.js, and Java, and supports development workflows including AI agents.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Self-hosted runner version enforcement date has moved
item.description:
GitHub has moved the enforcement date for minimum version requirements on self-hosted runners in GitHub Actions for GitHub Enterprise Cloud. The change ships on Monday, September 28, 2026, with full enforcement starting after that date.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure SQL Managed Instance updates for late-September 2026
item.description:
Azure SQL Managed Instance received late-September 2026 updates, including a flexible memory feature that lets you change the memory allocated to an instance without changing the instance size.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Claude Sonnet 5.5 in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
Claude Sonnet 5.5 is now generally available in GitHub Copilot. GitHub says it is intended for well-scoped everyday tasks such as building features and fixing bugs.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Luxembourg - Azure Extended Zones
item.description:
Microsoft announced general availability of the Luxembourg Azure Extended Zone. Azure Extended Zones are small-footprint Azure extensions designed for low-latency workloads and data residency requirements in specific metro areas or jurisdictions.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: dotnet: Build Agentic UI with the new Blazor AI components
item.description:
Microsoft announced new Blazor AI components for building agentic UI in .NET. The components target streamed content, tool use, approvals, shared state, and generative experiences.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: security: NeedyMantis: Unpacking a post-compromise malware family used in targeted operations
item.description:
Microsoft Threat Intelligence identified NeedyMantis, a modular post-compromise malware framework used in targeted intrusions. It uses custom loaders, encrypted archives, and extensible components to keep access and support follow-on activity.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Enterprise managed settings in-product validator
item.description:
GitHub Copilot now includes an in-product validator for enterprise managed settings. It checks for malformed JSON, unsupported configurations, invalid team mappings, and similar issues that could block settings from working correctly.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Usage metrics API adds pull request review stages
item.description:
GitHub’s enterprise and organization repository-level Copilot usage metrics reports now include pull request review stage timing. Each repos-1-day row gets a new pull_request_review_times array with time spent in each review stage.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Private saved views for repository issues and “Relates to” issue relationship is generally available
item.description:
GitHub repository issues now support private saved views, allowing users to save personalized issue filters and layouts. The “Relates to” issue relationship is also generally available.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Changes to query results in the GitHub Actions API and UI
item.description:
GitHub Actions workflow run queries in the API and UI now return a less precise but more accurate total count for search results across filters like workflow, event, status, and branch.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure HorizonDB supports PostgreSQL 18
item.description:
Azure HorizonDB is now in public preview with PostgreSQL 18 support. The service is a fully managed, PostgreSQL-compatible cloud-native database for scalable, high-performance workloads.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Agentic autofix now uses Copilot Memory
item.description:
Agentic autofix now checks Copilot Memory when that feature is enabled, using existing memories as context to help resolve security alerts.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: AG-UI Protocol now has a first-class .NET SDK
item.description:
Microsoft released a first-class .NET SDK for the AG-UI protocol. It lets .NET services expose and consume interoperable agent endpoints through Microsoft.Extensions.AI.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — September 21
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s weekly release roundup adds new models, local sandboxing in the Copilot app, and updates across Copilot integrations in Slack, Microsoft Teams, JetBrains, and VS Code.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Updates to GitHub Copilot for Slack and Microsoft Teams
item.description:
GitHub Copilot in Slack and Microsoft Teams has been updated to provide more context, more control, and a clearer path from chat conversations to GitHub work. The changelog does not include specific feature details in the provided text.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Storm-3168: Agentic-driven cloud attacks using compromised service principals
item.description:
Microsoft describes Azure attacks linked to Storm-3168 using compromised service principals, including reconnaissance, resource deletion, and credential access. The post links the activity to JADEPUFFER and includes defender guidance.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: CodeQL 2.27.1 adds C and C++ query and Kotlin 2.4.20 support
item.description:
CodeQL 2.27.1 adds new queries for C/C++ and C#, support for Kotlin 2.4.20, and query-accuracy improvements. It is the static analysis engine used by GitHub code scanning.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Default Enablement of Copilot Features for Copilot Business and Enterprise
item.description:
GitHub is introducing a global default policy that enables generally available Copilot features and supported client capabilities in enterprise and organization Copilot settings. The change takes effect over a 28-day window.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Require proof of presence for high-impact actions
item.description:
GitHub Enterprise Cloud now supports requiring proof of presence before members perform high-impact actions. This adds an interactive re-authentication or MFA challenge on top of the existing sudo-style control.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: ai: Control where your hosted agent connects with network egress in Foundry Agent Service
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry Agent Service now supports outbound network egress controls for hosted agents. You can define and attach an outbound policy, then monitor allowed and denied calls in Audit or Enforced mode.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: azure: Retirement: Azure Communication Services (ACS) standalone services will be retired on September 30, 2028
item.description:
Microsoft will retire several standalone Azure Communication Services offerings on September 30, 2028. After that date, the affected services will no longer be available.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: commandline: Introducing run-assert-eval: Find the risk, fix it, prove it
item.description:
Microsoft introduced run-assert-eval, a skill for runtime risk discovery in agents. It identifies relevant risks, measures failure rates, generates a runtime policy from the results, and reruns evaluation to verify the fix.

  • Source: Microsoft Command Line Blog

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Instant Access for VM restore points
item.description:
Instant Access for application-consistent restore points on Azure virtual machines is now generally available. It lets you start restoring a disk from a restore point before the underlying snapshot copy completes, for VMs using Premium SSD v2 or Ultra disks as data disks.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: Beyond the ransomware: Tracking Storm-2570’s consistent tradecraft across deployments
item.description:
Microsoft says Storm-2570 reuses the same post-compromise tools and techniques across multiple ransomware deployments, including Qilin, DragonForce, Anubis, and BERT. The post outlines guidance for defenders to detect and disrupt the activity before ransomware is deployed.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: security: ​​​​​​​​What’s new in Microsoft Security: September 2026​​
item.description:
Microsoft Security’s September 2026 update focuses on discovering and controlling local AI agents, extending Zero Trust controls to agent traffic, and improving SOC foundational capabilities.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: ai: From Chatbots to Automated Agents: Routines in Microsoft Foundry Are Now Generally Available
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry’s Routines feature is now generally available, adding event-driven and scheduled automation so agents can monitor work, react to business events, and continue tasks over time instead of only responding in chat.

  • Source: Microsoft AI Foundry Blog

item.title: github: More ways to request and configure Copilot code reviews
item.description:
GitHub Copilot code review now supports more personal configuration options, is available to a broader set of Copilot plans, and adds an enterprise-level default setting. These changes are generally available.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Node 20 is no longer available in GitHub Actions
item.description:
GitHub Actions runners no longer include Node 20. JavaScript actions now run on Node 24, and the temporary ACTIONS_ALLOW_USE_UNSECURE_NODE_VERSION opt-out is no longer available.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: Microsoft is updating its author-signing certificate starting September 23, 2026
item.description:
Microsoft will update the author-signing certificate used for NuGet packages on September 23, 2026. Users who rely on trusted signer policies or certificate fingerprint verification should add the new certificate before then.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: azure: Retirement: Support for PowerShell 7.4 ends on November 10, 2026
item.description:
Support for PowerShell 7.4 ends on November 10, 2026. Azure Function apps using 7.4 will keep running, but security updates and customer support stop, so users should move to PowerShell 7.6.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: Retirement: Support for .NET 8 and .NET 9 ends on November 10, 2026—upgrade your apps to .NET 10
item.description:
Support for .NET 8 and .NET 9 in Azure Functions ends on November 10, 2026. Apps will keep running, but they will no longer receive security updates or support for those runtimes, so migrate to .NET 10 before the deadline.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: Reimagining the SOC for the agentic era in Microsoft Defender
item.description:
Microsoft announced ISOC in Microsoft Defender, a foundation for agentic security that combines SIEM and threat protection capabilities in one place. The post positions this as part of reworking the SOC for agentic-era operations.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Local sandboxing in the GitHub Copilot app
item.description:
GitHub Copilot app now supports local sandboxing to limit the impact of unintended commands by restricting access to local files, network resources, and credentials. The feature is configured in the app.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: OpenTelemetry in the GitHub Copilot app
item.description:
The GitHub Copilot app now supports OpenTelemetry configuration via enterprise-managed settings. This lets organizations observe Copilot agent performance and interactions with models and tools.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: New features and improvements in Copilot for JetBrains
item.description:
GitHub Copilot for JetBrains 1.18.0 adds AI-assisted tool approvals, more control over agent conversations, and organization-wide shared skills and instructions. It also includes plan review support with Codex.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Faster C++ code intelligence with whole codebase indexing
item.description:
GitHub Copilot CLI now supports whole-codebase indexing for C++ repositories, improving code intelligence performance. The change is aimed at large C++ codebases with many interconnected files.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: Retirement: Support for Node.js 22 ends on April 30, 2027
item.description:
Support for Node.js 22 in Azure Functions ends on April 30, 2027. Apps will keep running, but security patches, updates, and support for Node.js 22 will stop; move to Node.js 24 by then.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Flex Nodes for AKS
item.description:
Flex Nodes for AKS is now in public preview. It lets application and platform teams use hybrid and edge infrastructure as connected worker nodes to an AKS control plane in Azure, while keeping a consistent Kubernetes control plane.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: k8s: Spotlight on SIG Apps
item.description:
SIG Apps is working on workload controller reliability, node lifecycle handling, and new patterns for AI and distributed workloads while preserving backward compatibility. The article highlights current focus areas, the trade-offs in changing core APIs, and a proposed Job API update for Kubernetes 1.38.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: github: Claude Opus 5.5 is now available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
Claude Opus 5.5 is now available in GitHub Copilot. GitHub says it can be used for agentic coding, long-running agentic tasks, and knowledge work.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: Creating a memory dump in C#
item.description:
The post describes how to create a memory dump from a C# application for debugging. It focuses on capturing the app’s state so it can be analyzed later.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: OpenAI’s GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna now available
item.description:
GitHub Copilot now includes two additional OpenAI GPT-6 models: GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna. They join the previously available GPT-6 Astra as selectable model options.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Unmasking EvilTokens: Getting to the root of device code phishing
item.description:
Microsoft says EvilTokens emerged as a major phishing-as-a-service platform for device code phishing, using AI-assisted lures, automated infrastructure, and token theft. In collaboration with partners, Microsoft’s Digital Crimes Unit disrupted its infrastructure and operations.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: devops+ai: Full SDLC in a Single Skill Command
item.description:
The article title and subtitle suggest a workflow for managing the full software development lifecycle from Jira to production using a single command and a team of automated agents. No technical implementation details are provided in the excerpt.

  • Source: Let’s do DevOps

item.title: github: Security improvements for SSH
item.description:
GitHub is updating SSH security by removing several older algorithms, adding a new one, and requiring larger RSA SSH keys. The change tightens supported SSH configurations to improve security.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Deprecation notice: All-platform CodeQL bundle
item.description:
GitHub has deprecated the all-platform CodeQL bundle starting with CodeQL CLI 2.27.0. The deprecated artifacts are codeql-bundle.tar.gz and codeql-bundle.tar.zst, which previously included binaries for all supported platforms.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Refreshed repository pull requests page generally available
item.description:
GitHub has generally available a refreshed repository pull requests page for all users. The update is intended to make pull requests easier to find and act on from one place.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Enterprise adds credential inventory exports
item.description:
GitHub Enterprise now lets enterprise owners export a complete inventory of credentials that can access the enterprise. The export includes SSH keys, classic and fine-grained personal access tokens, OAuth App access tokens, and other credential types.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Sphere OS version 26.09 is now available
item.description:
Azure Sphere OS version 26.09 is now available in the Retail feed. This release updates only the OS; there is no SDK update, and internet-connected devices will receive it from the cloud.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: Tracking When a PersistentVolumeClaim Was Last Used (Beta)
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 promotes PersistentVolumeClaimUnusedSinceTime to Beta and enables it by default. PVCs now get an Unused condition in status so you can tell whether any running or pending pod references the claim, and use lastTransitionTime to see when it last became idle.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Introducing a Guided Copilot Experience for Building Azure Apps in VS Code
item.description:
Microsoft is previewing a guided Copilot experience in VS Code for building Azure apps. It provides a structured workflow that helps move from idea to deployed app instead of relying on a free-form chat session.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Azure Functions support for PowerShell 7.6
item.description:
Azure Functions now generally supports PowerShell 7.6. Apps can be developed locally with PowerShell 7.6 and deployed to Azure Functions plans.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Grok 4.7 is now available in GitHub Copilot
item.description:
Grok 4.7 is rolling out in GitHub Copilot. GitHub describes it as xAI’s latest reasoning model, intended for agentic coding and complex multistep workflows.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot code review: An improved review experience
item.description:
GitHub updated Copilot code review to make review changes easier to track over time, auto-resolve more of its own suggestions, and generate commit messages when suggestions are accepted.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Manage the code coverage ruleset condition with the REST API
item.description:
GitHub now supports managing the “Restrict code coverage” repository ruleset option through the generally available REST API, in addition to the existing UI. This lets admins enforce code coverage requirements programmatically.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: GitHub Copilot weekly releases — September 14
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s weekly release adds new model selection options, updates to code review, and Sentry integration in the Copilot app. The post also mentions additional admin updates and new agent features.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Foundry Routines in Foundry Agent Service
item.description:
Foundry Agent Service now includes Foundry Routines in public preview. This adds a native trigger primitive so published agents can run automatically on schedules or in response to business events.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Upcoming deprecation of selected GitHub Copilot models in mid-October
item.description:
GitHub will deprecate selected Copilot models across all Copilot experiences on October 19, 2026. The affected models include those used in Copilot Chat, inline edits, ask and agent modes, and code completions.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Mdsv4 and Msv4 Series Virtual Machines for SAP
item.description:
Azure announced public preview availability of the Mdsv4 and Msv4 memory-optimized virtual machine series for SAP. The series uses 6th Generation Intel Xeon Scalable processors and includes advanced security features plus Azure Boost technologies.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Enable and disable controls for Microsoft Foundry agents in Agent 365
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry agents can now be enabled or disabled from the Agent 365 governance surface in Microsoft Admin Center, and the feature is generally available. Administrators can control whether a Foundry agent is available for use across the tenant.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Network egress controls for hosted agents in Microsoft Foundry
item.description:
Microsoft Foundry public preview now supports network egress controls for hosted agents. Customers can define ordered outbound rules by destination host, including wildcard FQDNs like *.contoso.com, with allow or deny actions.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Publishing Microsoft Foundry agents to Microsoft 365 Copilot and Teams
item.description:
Publishing Microsoft Foundry agents to Microsoft 365 Copilot and Teams is now generally available. This gives Foundry developers a native path to make agents operational in the Microsoft 365 surfaces where users work.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Logical replication slot sync status metric for Azure PostgreSQL Flexible Server
item.description:
Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server now includes a new Azure Monitor metric, logical_replication_slot_sync_status, to track the synchronization status of logical replication slots. It is generally available and lets you monitor whether each logical replication slot is in sync.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Stage-only npm tokens for safer automation
item.description:
GitHub added a new npm granular access token permission option, Read and write (stage only). It allows automated workflows to stage package versions for review without granting the token full publish access.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: New and improved troubleshooting guides for Azure Database for PostgreSQL
item.description:
Updated troubleshooting guidance is now available for Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server. The documentation adds expanded diagnostics for high CPU, memory, IOPS, temporary file usage, and autovacuum issues to help identify root causes.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: PG18 support for Azure Database for PostgreSQL elastic clusters
item.description:
Azure Database for PostgreSQL elastic clusters now support PostgreSQL 18. The update is available generally and is intended for new or existing distributed, cloud-scale workloads.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: github: Copilot impact dashboard now shows feature engagement
item.description:
The Copilot impact dashboard now includes feature engagement data, showing how many active users regularly use key Copilot features. Enterprise administrators can use it to identify widely adopted experiences and those that may need more attention.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Agentic CLI customizations now in the usage metrics API
item.description:
GitHub Copilot’s usage metrics API now includes agentic CLI activity for skills, custom agents, MCP servers, slash commands, and plugins. This extends existing CLI report coverage with additional customization metrics.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure Payments HSM v2
item.description:
Azure Payments HSM v2 is in public preview. It is a highly available, single-tenant payment HSM service for payment processing, credential issuance, PIN processing, key management, and authentication data protection, with exclusive administrative control retained by the customer.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: High-scale mesh in Azure Virtual Network Manager
item.description:
High-scale mesh connectivity with connected groups in Azure Virtual Network Manager is now generally available. In supported regions, a single mesh connectivity configuration can connect up to 3,000 virtual networks by default, with higher scale IP connectivity available.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: security: From guidance to action: Security fundamentals that materially reduce risk
item.description:
Microsoft says AI has changed the cybersecurity operating environment and points readers to exposure management guidance with recommended controls. The post emphasizes taking action on security fundamentals to reduce risk.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Ubuntu 26 generally available and latest migration
item.description:
Ubuntu 26.04 runner images for GitHub Actions are now generally available and fully supported for production workflows on x64 and arm64. The release notes also mention a migration update.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: security: Improving email security outcomes with real-world Microsoft Defender insights
item.description:
Microsoft says its latest email security benchmarking reports show strong Defender performance in both pre-delivery and post-delivery scenarios. The post also notes ongoing changes in how threats and defenses are evolving.

  • Source: Microsoft Security Blog

item.title: github: Workflow execution protections in GitHub Actions generally available
item.description:
Workflow execution protections in GitHub Actions are now generally available for GitHub Enterprise, organizations, and repositories. The feature lets you define an allowlist to control who can execute workflows.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: dotnet: Build Your Own AI Agent Harness in C#, the MafClaw Live Series
item.description:
Microsoft is running a 4-part live series showing how to build a C# AI agent harness with Microsoft Agent Framework, starting from a single IChatClient call and evolving it into a production-ready agent with observability and governance. The post is an announcement for the series and does not include technical implementation details.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: github: Automate SSO authorization for classic PATs and SSH keys
item.description:
GitHub Enterprise Cloud now lets enterprise admins automate SSO authorization for existing classic PATs and SSH keys across organizations, removing the need for developers to authorize each org manually.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: SCIM user responses now include a profileUrl attribute
item.description:
GitHub SCIM user responses now include the RFC 7643 standard profileUrl attribute. It returns the absolute URL of the GitHub account linked to the external identity.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: github: Copilot budget increase requests are generally available
item.description:
GitHub Copilot now supports a request flow for users who have exhausted their AI credits, allowing them to ask for a budget increase instead of being fully blocked from credit-consuming features. The feature is now generally available.

  • Source: GitHub

item.title: k8s: Kubernetes v1.37: Hardening Container Storage with Bind Mount Options and EmptyDir Permissions
item.description:
Kubernetes v1.37 adds alpha support for bind mount options on volume mounts and configurable permission modes for emptyDir volumes. These features let users apply Linux mount flags like noexec, nosuid, and nodev, and set emptyDir modes such as 01777 or 0750 without init-container workarounds.

  • Source: Kubernetes Official Blog

item.title: azure: Retirement Update: SAP container images removed October 14, 2026
item.description:
SAP container images are scheduled for removal on October 14, 2026. The containerized SAP data connector retired on September 14, 2026 and is now unsupported and unmaintained, though existing TLS-compliant agents can still send logs through the retired HTTP Data Collector API.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [In preview] Public Preview: Azure SQL updates for mid-September 2026
item.description:

item.title: GitHub Copilot FinOps: From License Management to AI Cost Governance
item.description:
For the past two years, most GitHub Copilot conversations have focused on productivity.

How much faster can developers code?

How many pull requests can be completed?

How much time can engineering teams save?

These are important questions.

But they are no longer the only questions that matter.

With the introduction of AI Credits, usage-based billing, user-level budgets, expanding model choice, agentic workflows, and autonomous development experiences, GitHub Copilot has evolved from a developer productivity tool into something larger: a platform that requires financial governance.

item.title: 🧰 Claude vs Copilot in VS Code: Meet the Harness
item.description:

That reading is wrong, and it leads to bad comparisons. The list is not about models. It is about agent harnesses. Once you separate the two, a lot of confusing behaviour starts to make sense, including why the same Claude model can feel like a different tool depending on where you run it.

item.title: 🤖 Azure AI Services in 2026: What to Use and When
item.description:
If you have seen the “Azure AI Services Explained” visual, you already know the core idea: Azure gives you purpose-built AI services for seeing, hearing, reading, translating, extracting, searching, generating, and protecting content.

The challenge in 2026 is not access to AI capabilities. It is choosing the right service mix quickly and avoiding legacy paths that are no longer ideal for new builds.

Core Azure AI services most teams start with

  • Azure AI Vision for image and video analysis, OCR, and visual understanding.
  • Azure AI Speech for speech-to-text, text-to-speech, translation, and speaker scenarios.
  • Azure AI Language for NLP tasks like sentiment, entities, summarization, and intent extraction.
  • Azure AI Translator for multilingual text translation.
  • Azure AI Document Intelligence for extracting structured data from forms and documents.
  • Azure AI Search for keyword, vector, semantic, and hybrid retrieval (critical for RAG).
  • Azure AI Content Safety for harmful and policy-violating content detection.
  • Azure OpenAI Service for LLM-based chat, generation, reasoning, and embeddings.
  • Azure Machine Learning for custom model lifecycle, MLOps, and enterprise deployment.
  • Azure AI Foundry Model Catalog for model discovery and deployment across providers.
  • Azure AI Foundry Agent Service for tool-using agents with orchestration and memory.
  • Azure Content Understanding for multimodal reasoning across document, image, audio, and video.

ValueTask vs Task

Task is a reference type allocated on the heap. In ultra‑hot paths where many calls complete synchronously, ValueTask can save allocations.

public async ValueTask<int> GetNumberAsync(bool cached)
{
 if (cached) return 42; // completes synchronously (no allocation)
 await Task.Delay(1000); // completes asynchronously
 return 42;
}

Guidelines

  • Prefer Task by default (simpler, safer).
  • Consider ValueTask when profiling shows allocation pressure and many sync completions.
  • Don’t await a ValueTask more than once and don’t store it; convert to Task via .AsTask() if you must pass it around.

As cloud-native services increasingly move into the public sphere, identity has emerged as the new defensive perimeter—if an attacker compromises your identities and credentials, they’re essentially inside.

Why Identities Matter More Than Ever

If you’ve participated in a cybersecurity roundtable recently, you’ve likely heard someone mention, “Identity is the new perimeter.” Historically, once you were inside a corporate network, you had broad access to internal systems—much like walking through a front door and freely wandering the house. However, the widespread adoption of cloud services—accessible from anywhere—has turned this model upside down.

What is Load Balancing?

Load balancing is the even distribution of network traffic across a group of backend computing resources or servers. The primary goals of load balancing are:

✅ Optimizing resource utilization
✅ Maximizing throughput & performance
✅ Minimizing response time
✅ Ensuring high availability
✅ Preventing overload on a single resource

In Azure, there are multiple load-balancing options, each designed for different traffic types and use cases.
